overview: Two ways twins can form, differing in whether they come from one fertilised egg that splits, or two separately fertilised eggs.
genZNote: Identical twins: one zygote that decided to become two. Fraternal twins: two separate eggs that just happened to share a due date.

aspects.label: Origin
aspects.valueA: A single fertilised egg (zygote) that splits into two embryos early in development.
aspects.valueB: Two separate eggs, each fertilised by a different sperm.

aspects.label: Genetic Similarity
aspects.valueB: Genetically as similar as regular siblings (share about 50% of DNA on average).

aspects.label: Sex of Twins
aspects.valueB: Can be the same sex or different sexes.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Monozygotic (identical) twins are always the same sex because they come from a single zygote; dizygotic (fraternal) twins can be either.
overlay.memoryTrick: Mono = one zygote splits (identical). Di = two separate zygotes (fraternal).
overlay.commonMisconception: Identical twins are not 100% identical in every trait later in life — environmental factors and epigenetic differences can still cause them to differ.
